newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore productivity drop no concern - minister.
newsitem.headline: Singapore productivity drop no concern - minister.

text.p: Singapore's Minister for Trade and Industry Lee Yock Suan said on Wednesday that a drop in Singapore's productivity levels in 1996 was no cause for concern unless a trend emerged over several years.
"Just looking at this one figure, I'm not too concerned," he told reporters.
"Of course over the longer run if we see continuing low productivity we should be worried," he said.
Lee's ministry said on Tuesday that productivity growth in 1996 slowed to 0.7 percent from 3.6 percent the previous year.
Officials said this was a temporary blip and forecast productivity growth of about 4.0 percent in the medium term.
Trade has become a vital part of Singapore's economy and its increasing diversification and complexity brought new challenges to managing it, said Lee.
"I think we are doing very well in two particular areas -- electronics and chemicals -- and we continue to do well as a financial centre," he said.
But Lee added there was room to add new disciplines in the financial sector, to help it become more competitive against other centres like Hong Kong.
